rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design — no human backstops.

The only human check present is push-back on the result (L30-31), not a backstop replacing agent judgment on the retro flow itself. Harm the rule guards (paternalistic human-in-the-loop micromanagement) is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pattern-recognition LOs need n≥2 instances with contrast.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No multi-participant attribution concern; this is a single student's own session and repo.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Nothing is written over.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No shared room record being written to in this exercise; the compound prompt explicitly requires integrate-not-append into the student's own file, a different (personal, non-room) concern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Filing is invisible.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No participant-files-into-a-folder beat exists here; not a group workshop surface.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Scope-of-sharing is declared before contribution, not after.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No tiered room-contribution-sharing mechanic in this individual exercise (the personal-vs-team promotion question in check_pedagogy §18 is a different, single-student mechanic, not a room-scale sharing tier).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A decision beat needs a real constraint.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The push-back and gitignore-keep-or-revert beats are individual student decisions, not a group decision beat requiring a room-scale constraint.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Group decisions are human, and named as such.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No group decision is being made in this exercise; every accept/reject/keep/revert call is one student's own judgment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Retrospective = group round, no prompts, trainer silent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file's retro is an individual student-and-agent retro (a different, single-participant sense of "retro"), not a room-scale group round.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Second-facilitator test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a room-scale beat requiring a second-facilitator handoff test; the maintainer block's leap test and per-phase failure-mode table already carry the trainer-delivery mechanics an individual exercise needs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the too-big and too-small room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No group beat with a room-size breaking point exists here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mixed-experience is the default room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No beat here assumes prior-participant pairing or shared room experience; each student works their own repo and session independently.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Room beats overrun; name the protected beat.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single 15-minute individual exercise, not a room-scale beat needing a protected/cut designation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No mechanical coverage - the trainer guide carries the load.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a room-scale beat; this exercise IS mechanically coverable (prompts, prose) and is in fact covered by the ordinary per-file judge classes.
